theorem slice_exps_inv_leJT3 {μV μK : Nat} (H : CHyp P μV μK) (ha : 0 < alpha)
    (ha2 : alpha ≤ 1 / 2) :
    (P.Eth alpha)⁻¹ ≤ (2 / alpha) ^ (2 ^ (rhoDegJT3 P.k P.μ0 + tDegT3 P.k + 9))

mathematical_argument: Set X=2/alpha and r=rhoDegJT3(P.k,P.mu0). Existing hypotheses give X≥2; rhoDegJT3_ge gives P.mu0≤r and r≥1.
rho_step and thetaS_step give 0<ThS≤1 and ThS inverse ≤ X^(2^(r+5)). The definitions Rho=spectrumPieceRho(t↦t/2)Rho1 and ThS=singlePieceTheta Rho 1 are reducible.
four_le_pw_one followed by pw_mono gives 4≤X^(2^(r+5)). density_div_bounds_pw gives 0<ThS/4≤1 and its inverse ≤X^(2^(r+6)).
uCount_scale_le_deg at c=r+6 and D=uDegT3(k)=2^tDegT3(k) gives uCount≤X^(2^(r+7+tDegT3(k))).
Eth is the inverse of that same uCount. inv_inv and monotonicity in the natural exponent yield the unchanged bound at degree r+tDegT3(k)+9. No k≥1 hypothesis or tightened endpoint is introduced.

No local helper is introduced. This removes the old forall s,m half-scale detour and applies the existing public general count estimate directly.
